--- title: "Offensive linemen are drafted most often and quarterbacks earliest" date: "2026-10-24" author: - "An AI directed by Nick Giangreco" freeze: auto vignette: > %\VignetteIndexEntry{Offensive linemen are drafted most often and quarterbacks earliest} %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html} %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8} --- ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Load cfbstats from the checkout when the package is not installed, so the # site build does not require a package install (decision 0030). if (requireNamespace("cfbstats", quietly = TRUE)) { library(cfbstats) } else { dir <- getwd() while (!file.exists(file.path(dir, "_targets")) && dirname(dir) != dir) { dir <- dirname(dir) } for (src in sort(list.files( file.path(dir, "R"), pattern = "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE ))) { source(src, local = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8") } } library(DBI) library(dplyr) library(duckdb) library(ggiraph) library(ggplot2) library(knitr) library(tibble) library(tidyr) # altdoc renders in a temp dir; point the knit wd at the project root so # data/*.parquet and tar_read() resolve (CFBSTATS_ROOT is set in the site build). root <- cfbstats_root() if (nzchar(root)) { knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root) } set_girafe_defaults( opts_hover = opts_hover( css = "stroke:#111827;stroke-width:2.5px;filter:brightness(1.12);" ), opts_hover_inv = opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.45;"), opts_tooltip = opts_tooltip( css = "background:#111827;color:#fff;padding:6px 9px;border-radius:5px;font-weight:bold;font-size:15px;" ), opts_zoom = opts_zoom(min = 1, max = 5), opts_toolbar = opts_toolbar(saveaspng = TRUE, position = "topright"), opts_sizing = opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE) ) # Wilson interval for a binomial proportion. wilson <- function(x, n, z = 1.96) { p <- x / n d <- 1 + z^2 / n c <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / d h <- (z / d) * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) c(lo = pmax(0, c - h), hi = pmin(1, c + h)) } ``` ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} *Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-10-24. Draft classes after the last complete draft are right-censored and carry no outcomes, so they are excluded from every rate below rather than counted as failures. Each season's position comes from the roster table, joined by athlete id and season.* ::: ## 1. Introduction The previous post measured how often eligible college seasons end in an NFL outcome, over the whole population at once. But nobody watches football that way. The draft broadcasts positional differences every spring: quarterbacks and pass rushers go early, punters appear once, late, on a conference call. Position is also the first thing any draft model would condition on, so the rates need tabulating where they actually vary. This post splits those eligible player-seasons by the position the player lined up at in that season, and asks five questions: + *Expecting quarterbacks to be the most draftable position* + *Expecting first-round picks to concentrate among quarterbacks* + *Expecting quarterbacks to be picked earliest on average, in every draft class* + *Expecting the per-season chance of NFL entry to rise with waiting, for every position* + *Expecting quarterbacks to arrive through the draft while other positions lean on the undrafted route* Each question is a claim the data can settle, answered with a table or figure backed by an assertion. ## 2. Data and terms The unit is the same as before: a **player-season**, one player's college season with a recorded stat line. Rates are computed over **eligible player-seasons**, seasons whose following draft the player could have been selected in. Draft classes whose outcomes may occur in the future are excluded rather than counted as misses. Each season carries the roster position the player was listed at that season; a few carry none and form their own group in Table 1. Roster listings use two dozen shorthand codes, from QB to LS, and neighboring codes describe the same professional role. The analysis groups them into nine reader-facing groups, plus a tenth row for the seasons with none recorded. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} group_terms <- tribble( ~Group , ~"Roster codes in the group" , "Quarterback" , "QB" , "Running back" , "RB, FB" , "Receiver" , "WR" , "Tight end" , "TE" , "Offensive line" , "T, G, C, OL" , "Defensive line" , "DL, DE, DT, NT, EDGE" , "Linebacker" , "LB, ILB, OLB" , "Defensive back" , "DB, S, CB" , "Special teams" , "PK, P, LS, PR" , "Position not recorded" , "Seasons whose roster entry carries no usable position code, including the rare ATH listing (concentrated in earlier draft classes), or no roster row at all" ) kable(group_terms, caption = "Table 1: the position groups used throughout") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Table 1: the position groups used throughout |Group |Roster codes in the group | |:---------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |Quarterback |QB | |Running back |RB, FB | |Receiver |WR | |Tight end |TE | |Offensive line |T, G, C, OL | |Defensive line |DL, DE, DT, NT, EDGE | |Linebacker |LB, ILB, OLB | |Defensive back |DB, S, CB | |Special teams |PK, P, LS, PR | |Position not recorded |Seasons whose roster entry carries no usable position code, including the rare ATH listing (concentrated in earlier draft classes), or no roster row at all | ::: ::: A note on the uncertainty intervals: whenever a percentage is reported below, it comes with a 95 percent confidence interval, the range the true rate plausibly occupies given how many seasons were observed. The style is Wilson's, chosen because it behaves well for rare events like these. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # The connection message is an implementation detail; the reader sees only # the counts in the visible chunks. con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), "data/cfbstats.duckdb", read_only = TRUE) outcomes <- tbl(con, "outcomes") |> collect() roster_pos <- tbl(con, "roster") |> # A few players carry two roster rows in one season (mid-season moves); # they always agree on the position, so one row per player-season is kept. select(playerId, season, position) |> distinct() |> collect() dbDisconnect(con) risk <- outcomes |> filter(draft_eligible, outcome_observed_d) |> mutate( across( c(outcome_drafted_d, outcome_signed_udfa_d, outcome_nfl_entry_d), ~ coalesce(.x, FALSE) ) ) |> left_join(roster_pos, by = c("playerId", "season")) pos_group <- c( QB = "Quarterback", RB = "Running back", FB = "Running back", WR = "Receiver", TE = "Tight end", T = "Offensive line", G = "Offensive line", C = "Offensive line", OL = "Offensive line", DL = "Defensive line", DE = "Defensive line", DT = "Defensive line", NT = "Defensive line", EDGE = "Defensive line", LB = "Linebacker", ILB = "Linebacker", OLB = "Linebacker", DB = "Defensive back", S = "Defensive back", CB = "Defensive back", PK = "Special teams", P = "Special teams", LS = "Special teams", PR = "Special teams" ) n_risk_pre <- nrow(risk) risk <- risk |> mutate( group = dplyr::coalesce( dplyr::recode(position, !!!pos_group, .default = "Position not recorded"), "Position not recorded" ) ) n_risk <- nrow(risk) n_players <- n_distinct(risk$playerId) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} risk_set <- tibble( Measure = c("Eligible player-seasons", "Distinct players"), Count = format(c(n_risk, n_players), big.mark = ",") ) kable(risk_set, caption = "Table 2: the risk set") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Table 2: the risk set |Measure |Count | |:-----------------------|:------| |Eligible player-seasons |68,993 | |Distinct players |36,223 | ::: ::: Players move, and a player can carry a different code in a different season; each season is counted at the position it was played at. ## 3. Results ### 3.1 How often each position is drafted *Expecting quarterbacks to be the most draftable position.* ❌ **The expectation does not hold.** The quarterback row sits mid-table; the top belongs to the offensive line, the bottom to the specialists. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rates <- risk |> group_by(group) |> summarise( seasons = n(), players = n_distinct(playerId), drafted_ev = sum(outcome_drafted_d), entry_ev = sum(outcome_nfl_entry_d), .groups = "drop" ) |> dplyr::rowwise() |> mutate( drafted = drafted_ev / seasons, entry = entry_ev / seasons, drafted_lo = 100 * wilson(drafted_ev, seasons)["lo"], drafted_hi = 100 * wilson(drafted_ev, seasons)["hi"] ) |> arrange(desc(drafted)) rates_out <- rates |> transmute( `Position group` = group, `Eligible seasons` = format(seasons, big.mark = ","), `Players` = format(players, big.mark = ","), `Drafted` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * drafted), `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.1f%%, %.1f%%]", drafted_lo, drafted_hi), `NFL entry` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * entry) ) kable( rates_out, caption = "Table 3: drafted and NFL-entry prevalence by position group" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Table 3: drafted and NFL-entry prevalence by position group |Position group |Eligible seasons |Players |Drafted |95% CI |NFL entry | |:---------------------|:----------------|:-------|:-------|:-------------|:---------| |Offensive line |984 |806 |8.2% |[6.7%, 10.1%] |15.9% | |Position not recorded |869 |604 |5.1% |[3.8%, 6.7%] |11.0% | |Tight end |4,232 |2,266 |4.1% |[3.6%, 4.8%] |10.0% | |Defensive back |14,265 |7,476 |4.1% |[3.8%, 4.4%] |9.2% | |Defensive line |10,178 |5,268 |3.9% |[3.5%, 4.2%] |8.5% | |Quarterback |4,338 |2,197 |3.7% |[3.2%, 4.3%] |6.5% | |Running back |7,991 |4,109 |3.4% |[3.0%, 3.8%] |7.6% | |Receiver |12,472 |6,539 |3.3% |[3.0%, 3.7%] |8.6% | |Linebacker |9,255 |4,831 |3.3% |[2.9%, 3.6%] |7.8% | |Special teams |4,409 |2,325 |1.2% |[0.9%, 1.6%] |3.9% | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bars <- rates |> select(group, drafted, entry) |> pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "outcome", values_to = "p") |> mutate( outcome = dplyr::recode(outcome, drafted = "Drafted", entry = "NFL entry"), group = factor(group, levels = rev(rates$group)) ) p_rates <- ggplot(bars, aes(p, group, fill = outcome)) + geom_col_interactive( aes( tooltip = paste0( group, ", ", tolower(outcome), ": ", scales::percent(p, accuracy = 0.1) ) ), position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7 ) + scale_x_continuous( labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .05)) ) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("Drafted" = "#1B9E77", "NFL entry" = "gray55")) + theme_cfbstats() + labs( x = "Prevalence among eligible player-seasons", y = NULL, fill = NULL ) girafe(ggobj = p_rates, width_svg = 8, height_svg = 6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Out of every 100 eligible offensive-line seasons, about 8 end with the player drafted and 16 with the player reaching the NFL by any route, against 4 and 7 for quarterbacks and 1 and 4 for specialists. The drafted spread from top to bottom is more than sixfold. The offensive-line result deserves a qualifier that Section 5 returns to: linemen rarely record a statistic, and this population counts only seasons with a stat line, so the 8.2 percent is the draft rate of the small, selected minority of linemen who left one. ### 3.2 Where the first round goes *Expecting first-round picks to concentrate among quarterbacks.* ✅ **The expectation holds.** The recurring cast of this series is, as it happens, all quarterbacks: Joe Burrow first overall in 2020, Cameron Ward first overall in 2025, Jordan Travis in the fifth round in 2024, and Shane Buechele and Kyle Allen undrafted. The cast's one-position makeup is itself a hint at the shape of the first round. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} round_mix <- risk |> filter(outcome_drafted_d) |> group_by(group) |> summarise( drafted_seasons = n(), round1 = sum(outcome_draft_round_d == 1L), .groups = "drop" ) |> mutate(round1_share = round1 / drafted_seasons) |> arrange(desc(round1_share)) round_out <- round_mix |> transmute( `Position group` = group, `Drafted seasons` = format(drafted_seasons, big.mark = ","), `Of which round 1` = round1, `Round-1 share` = scales::percent(round1_share, accuracy = 0.1) ) kable( round_out, caption = "Table 4: the round-1 share of drafted seasons by position group" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Table 4: the round-1 share of drafted seasons by position group |Position group |Drafted seasons | Of which round 1|Round-1 share | |:---------------------|:---------------|----------------:|:-------------| |Quarterback |160 | 42|26.2% | |Defensive line |392 | 66|16.8% | |Offensive line |81 | 13|16.0% | |Receiver |415 | 59|14.2% | |Defensive back |583 | 72|12.3% | |Linebacker |302 | 32|10.6% | |Position not recorded |44 | 4|9.1% | |Tight end |175 | 13|7.4% | |Running back |273 | 16|5.9% | |Special teams |54 | 0|0.0% | ::: ::: When a quarterback does get drafted, the pick is a first-rounder 26.2 percent of the time, well ahead of the 16.8 percent of defensive linemen, the next group. The draft's most valuable resource, the early pick, is spent on one position disproportionately, while the back of the draft is where the running backs and specialists hear their names. A quarterback season is average in its chance of any pick and extreme in what that pick is worth. Both facts matter for modeling: the drafted label treats Burrow's first pick and Travis's 171st as the same event, and the position term is where a model can recover part of the difference. ### 3.3 Where in the draft each position lands, over the years *Expecting quarterbacks to be picked earliest on average, in every draft class.* ❌ **The expectation does not hold.** The measure is the average overall pick among each group's drafted seasons, across draft classes. Over the whole span quarterbacks do carry the lowest average, pick 112, with defensive linemen at 114 and specialists far back at 179. But the year-to-year ordering is noisy: quarterbacks are the lowest group in only 5 of the 14 draft classes. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pick_trend <- risk |> filter(outcome_drafted_d, !is.na(outcome_draft_pick_d)) |> group_by(group, draft_year) |> summarise( picks = n(), avg_pick = mean(outcome_draft_pick_d), .groups = "drop" ) |> filter(picks >= 5) p_pick <- ggplot( pick_trend, aes(draft_year, avg_pick, color = group) ) + geom_hline(yintercept = 126.6, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray70") + geom_line_interactive(linewidth = 1.1) + geom_point_interactive( aes( tooltip = paste0( group, ", ", draft_year, ": pick ", sprintf("%.0f", avg_pick), " on average (", picks, " picks)" ) ), size = 2.6 ) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2012, 2025, by = 2)) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) + scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") + theme_cfbstats() + labs( x = "Draft class", y = "Average overall pick among drafted seasons", color = NULL, caption = "Group-year cells with fewer than 5 picks omitted. Dashed line: average across all drafted seasons." ) girafe(ggobj = p_pick, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 5.5) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The instability has a mundane source: a class hands each position only a handful of picks, so one early selection moves a group's average by dozens of slots. The offensive line's cell appears only from 2018 on, the stat-line selection of Section 3.1 again, and swings from pick 58 to pick 170 on a dozen picks' worth of evidence. What survives year to year is the ordering at the extremes: quarterbacks and defensive linemen live in the first two rounds on average, running backs and specialists in the back half. ### 3.4 The per-season chance of entry, by position *Expecting the chance of NFL entry to rise with waiting, for every position.* ❌ **The expectation does not hold, for one group.** The measure is again the discrete-time hazard: among players still unentered after 1, 2, 3, ... eligible seasons, the share whose very next draft is the one that takes them. Every group with at least three published indices climbs over its first three; the offensive line publishes only two, and climbs over both. Special teams climbs to its third eligible season, then falls back. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} hazard <- risk |> group_by(group, eligible_season_index) |> summarise( seasons = n(), entry = mean(outcome_nfl_entry_d), .groups = "drop" ) |> filter(seasons >= 50) hazard_wide <- hazard |> select(group, eligible_season_index, entry) |> mutate(entry = scales::percent(entry, accuracy = 0.1)) |> pivot_wider( names_from = eligible_season_index, values_from = entry, names_prefix = "Season " ) kable( hazard_wide, caption = "Table 5: the per-season hazard of NFL entry by position group and eligible season index (indices with fewer than 50 seasons omitted)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Table 5: the per-season hazard of NFL entry by position group and eligible season index (indices with fewer than 50 seasons omitted) |group |Season 1 |Season 2 |Season 3 |Season 4 | |:---------------------|:--------|:--------|:--------|:--------| |Defensive back |4.5% |12.1% |18.4% |18.6% | |Defensive line |4.2% |9.7% |17.7% |23.3% | |Linebacker |3.8% |9.6% |15.9% |20.1% | |Offensive line |14.0% |24.2% |NA |NA | |Position not recorded |6.6% |16.5% |19.4% |NA | |Quarterback |2.6% |6.6% |15.5% |25.2% | |Receiver |4.1% |10.3% |20.0% |20.2% | |Running back |4.1% |9.4% |14.4% |18.6% | |Special teams |1.3% |4.7% |11.8% |8.1% | |Tight end |3.4% |13.3% |26.8% |28.3% | ::: ::: The climb is steep everywhere it happens. Quarterbacks go from 2.6 percent in their first eligible season to 25.2 percent at their fourth; tight ends reach 26.8 and 28.3 percent at their third and fourth seasons, the highest hazard in the table. The special-teams exception fits how that group is built: kickers and punters still unentered after three eligible seasons are increasingly the ones nobody was planning to draft, and the marginal fourth season does not change that. For the skill positions, an additional eligible season reads as accumulated proof, and the draft chance rises with it. ### 3.5 How each position reaches the NFL *Expecting quarterbacks to arrive through the draft while other positions lean on the undrafted route.* ✅ **The expectation holds.** Conditioning on the seasons that end in NFL entry, the undrafted share varies by position, and the ordering matches the fan's model of the sport. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} udfa_share <- risk |> filter(outcome_nfl_entry_d) |> group_by(group) |> summarise( entrants = n(), udfa = sum(outcome_signed_udfa_d), .groups = "drop" ) |> mutate(share = udfa / entrants) |> arrange(desc(share)) udfa_out <- udfa_share |> transmute( `Position group` = group, `Entrants` = format(entrants, big.mark = ","), `Arrived as UDFA` = scales::percent(share, accuracy = 0.1) ) kable( udfa_out, caption = "Table 6: the undrafted share of NFL entrants by position group" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Table 6: the undrafted share of NFL entrants by position group |Position group |Entrants |Arrived as UDFA | |:---------------------|:--------|:---------------| |Special teams |172 |68.6% | |Receiver |1,075 |61.4% | |Tight end |425 |58.8% | |Linebacker |723 |58.2% | |Defensive back |1,311 |55.5% | |Running back |607 |55.0% | |Defensive line |870 |54.9% | |Position not recorded |96 |54.2% | |Offensive line |156 |48.1% | |Quarterback |283 |43.5% | ::: ::: Among positions with real sample sizes, quarterbacks are the only group where the draft is the majority route: 43.5 percent of quarterback entrants arrived undrafted, against 61.4 percent for receivers and 68.6 percent for specialists. The overall figure from the previous post, 56.6 percent, sits between the extremes, and the position split explains part of why the aggregate looks the way it does. Buechele and Allen, the cast's two UDFA members, are both quarterbacks who entered through the minority route of their majority-drafted position. ## 4. Summary + The drafted rate spans from 8.2 percent of eligible offensive-line seasons down to 1.2 percent for special teams, a more than sixfold spread; quarterbacks sit mid-table at 3.7 percent. + Quarterbacks dominate the top of the draft: 26.2 percent of drafted quarterback seasons are first-round picks, well ahead of any other position's share. + Quarterbacks carry the lowest long-run average pick (112) among the groups with a cell in every draft class, but they are the year's lowest group in only 5 of 14 classes. + The per-season hazard of entry rises steeply with waiting for every group that publishes at least three indices; special teams peaks at eligible season three and falls back at season four. + Quarterbacks are the only position group whose entrants mostly arrive drafted (56.5 percent); for specialists the undrafted route carries 68.6 percent. ## 5. Discussion ::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal"} **The offensive line rate is a selection, not a fact about linemen.** This population requires a stat line, and linemen rarely appear in one. The 806 linemen in the risk set are those who recovered a fumble, caught a deflection, or otherwise left a statistical trace, and their 8.2 percent drafted rate describes that selected group. Models that use position should treat the line as a thin-data category, not the position with the best observed rate. ::: ::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal"} **Position is a feature the models should carry.** Both the level (a sixfold spread in drafted rates) and the shape (round mix, average pick, hazard timing, entry route) differ by position. A single pooled model would spend its capacity explaining variance that position names in one column. ::: Two caveats bound the figures. The not-recorded category holds 299 seasons, under half a percent of the risk set, concentrated in earlier draft classes whose roster entries lacked a usable position code, plus a few seasons with no roster row at all; their rates are reported but not compared. And the eligibility-clock imputation noted in the previous post applies here: high-school graduation year is imputed for players without a recruiting record, shifting rows in and out of the risk set. The shifts are not position-specific, so the between-group comparisons are sturdier than the absolute levels.
